newsitem.title: USA: IBM has 55 firms in virtual industrial park.
newsitem.headline: IBM has 55 firms in virtual industrial park.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp said that 55 small companies have joined its World Wide Web site designed for small businesses.
IBM said that its Web site, called World Distributor, is a secure site where small businesses can find and buy products, parts, machines and tools to run their business.

The site, which was started in September as a pilot program in conjunction with the National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors, is like a "virtual industrial park," IBM said. The only cost a company has is to maintain its own Web site, which is linked to the IBM World Distributor site.
IBM provides the secure encryption technology for companies to make purchases.
One small company, Carlson Systems of Omaha, Nebraska, is using World Distributor to enter new markets, reduce its cost of sales and improve its order processing, IBM said.

Full color customer catalogs are available online in areas including capital goods, chemicals, computer equipment, construction, consumer goods, foods and beverages, industrial parts and equipment, medical, metal and other categories.
